blocks.task_summary: Find the two values of b such that y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: vary b and observe when a stationary point of the cubic lies on the x-axis
determine b = 0 (when P(0, b) touches x-axis) and b = −4 (when local minimum at x = −2 touches x-axis)

evidence.basis: M1 for varying b with a = 3 or evidence that b = 0 case is considered; A1 for b = −4, 0.

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: deduce from part (a) that b < −4 or b > 0 gives exactly one x-intercept

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 + 3x^2 + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: deduce from part (a) that −4 < b < 0 gives exactly three x-intercepts

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly two x-axis intercepts.
method_path: determine that when a = −3, stationary points at x = 0 (y = b) and x = 2 (y = b − 4) give exactly two intercepts for b = 0, 4

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly one x-axis intercept.
method_path: deduce that b < 0 or b > 4 gives exactly one x-intercept

blocks.task_summary: Write the set of b values for which y = x^3 − 3x^2 + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: deduce that 0 < b < 4 gives exactly three x-intercepts

blocks.task_summary: For exactly three x-axis intercepts, state whether each point of zero gradient is above or below the x-axis.
method_path: state that the two stationary points lie on opposite sides of the x-axis

evidence.basis: A1 for 'one point of zero gradient is located on either side (of the x-axis)' or equivalent.

blocks.task_summary: Show that the curve has stationary points at P(0, b) and Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27 + b).
method_path: differentiate to obtain dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax
set dy/dx = 0 and factor to x(3x + 2a) = 0
solve to obtain x = 0 and x = −2a/3
verify P(0, b) is a stationary point and substitute x = −2a/3 into y = x³ + ax² + b
simplify to y = 4a³/27 + b to confirm Q(−2a/3, 4a³/27 + b)
accepted_alternatives: Substitute x = 0 and x = −2a/3 directly into dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax to verify each yields zero, then substitute x = −2a/3 into y = x³ + ax² + b and simplify to 4a³/27 + b (Method 2).

evidence.basis: Method 1: (A1) dy/dx = 3x² + 2ax; (M1) solve dy/dx = 0; (A1) x = 0, −2a/3; AG for P; (M1) substitute x into y; (A1) simplify to 4a³/27 + b. Method 2: (A1) dy/dx; (M1) substitute x=0 or x=−2a/3; AG for P; (A1) verify dy/dx=0 at both; (M1) substitute into y; (A1) simplify to y-coordinate.

blocks.task_summary: Find d²y/dx² and classify P and Q as local maximum or minimum when a > 0 and b > 0.
method_path: find d²y/dx² = 6x + 2a
evaluate at x = 0: d²y/dx² = 2a > 0 → P is a local minimum
evaluate at x = −2a/3: d²y/dx² = −2a < 0 → Q is a local maximum

evidence.basis: A1 for d²y/dx² = 6x + 2a; R1 for P is local minimum (2a > 0 when a > 0); R1 for Q is local maximum (−2a < 0 when a > 0).

blocks.task_summary: Determine whether P and Q are above or below the x-axis when a > 0 and b > 0.
method_path: note b > 0 and 4a³/27 + b > 0 when a > 0, b > 0, hence both P and Q lie above the x-axis

evidence.basis: A1 for both above the x-axis; accept a labelled sketch clearly showing this.

blocks.task_summary: For a < 0 and b > 0, state whether P is a local max or min and whether it is above or below the x-axis.
method_path: classify P as a local maximum (since a < 0 gives d²y/dx² = 2a < 0 at x = 0) and state it is above the x-axis (b > 0)

evidence.basis: A1 for P is a local maximum and is above the x-axis.

blocks.task_summary: State the conditions on a and b for Q to be below the x-axis.
method_path: state 4a³/27 + b < 0 or equivalently b < −4a³/27

evidence.basis: A1 for 4a³/27 + b < 0 or equivalent inequality, e.g. b < −4a³/27.

blocks.task_summary: Prove that if 4a³b + 27b² < 0 then y = x³ + ax² + b has exactly three x-axis intercepts.
method_path: factor 4a³b + 27b² < 0 as b(4a³ + 27b) < 0 or (b/27)(4a³ + 27b) < 0
deduce that b and (4a³/27 + b) have opposite signs
observe that b = y-coordinate of P and 4a³/27 + b = y-coordinate of Q
conclude P and Q lie on opposite sides of the x-axis
deduce that with stationary points on opposite sides the cubic must cross the x-axis exactly three times
accepted_alternatives: Split into two explicit cases: (1) b > 0 and 4a³/27 + b < 0 ⇒ a < 0 hence three intercepts; (2) b < 0 and 4a³/27 + b > 0 ⇒ a > 0 hence three intercepts (Method 2). The converse proof is also accepted for a maximum of 3 marks.

evidence.basis: Method 1: (M1) factor; (A1) b(4a³/27 + b) < 0 or (b)(4a³ + 27b) < 0; (A1) two sign cases; (R1) opposite signs ⇒ P and Q on opposite sides of x-axis; (R1) opposite sides ⇒ exactly three intercepts. Method 2: additional R1 for each subcase linking to sign of a.
